transcript:
John took a nap at his bedroom.
Birds can fly because they have wings.
We planned to visit her on next Monday.
The girl sat on the sofa.
Peter ran and fell on the floor.

errors.note: The preposition 'at' is typically used for specific locations, while 'in' is more appropriate for rooms.
The preposition 'on' is unnecessary before days of the week when using 'next'.
Using 'onto' instead of 'on' indicates movement towards the floor.
